sources.title: Human Ras–SOS exchange complex, Boriack-Sjodin et al. 1998

sources.title: Whitehurst et al. 2002, ERK2 nuclear entry
sources.supports: Permeabilized-cell import experiments support ERK2 entry through nuclear pore complexes and interaction with nucleoporins; no claim here that every cellular ERK route is carrier-independent.

findings.location: nuclear rim creation lines 140-144, doubleRim lines 190-198; ERK import lines 301-306
findings.evidence: Both nuclear rims are complete TorusGeometry objects. ERK center is interpolated across x=1.59 near the decorative pore, but no opening is made in either rim. MeshBVH triangle/triangle tests detect ERK/rim intersections at p=0.82, 0.835, 0.85, 0.86 and 0.88; four mesh-pair intersections at p=0.85. No-ligand and kinaseInactive branches do not import ERK. See evidence/signals/diagnostic.json:erk.
findings.whyWrong: The stage specifically teaches entry through a nuclear pore. The drawn pore does not replace the enclosing rim, so the displayed kinase crosses membrane material rather than a clear portal. This is a topological failure, not an objection to approximate molecular scale.
findings.fix: Give every nuclear-envelope layer an aligned open portal, size and route the existing ERK geometry through that portal with positive clearance, and keep inactive controls outside. Preserve the detailed kinase/pore geometry.
findings.verification: At representative and dense intermediate import samples, test actual ERK meshes against every nuclear membrane/rim triangle; assert no crossing outside the portal and correct pre/post compartment. Retain deterministic arbitrary seeks and condition regressions. Root should inspect normal-camera continuous entry.

sources.title: Lee et al. 2017, GATA1 nuclear marker
sources.supports: Primary immunohistochemical study reports strong nuclear GATA1 in immature erythroid precursors; supports nuclear regulator placement, not mouse-specific timing.

sources.title: Differential effects of GATA-1 on proliferation and differentiation of erythroid lineage cells
sources.supports: Primary study abstract describes conditional GATA-1 rescue of null embryonic-stem-cell primitive/definitive erythropoiesis; supports regulatory role. Repeated full-page retrieval was inconsistent.

sources.title: Wang et al. 2012, PI3K-dependent erythroblast polarization
sources.supports: Primary study abstract describes mouse fetal-liver erythroblasts, polarization and extrusion into membrane-enclosed nuclear bud. Full-page open encountered anti-bot challenge, so no newly asserted detailed mechanical conclusion relies on full text.

findings.location: GATA1 creation lines 88-107; position update lines 261-266
findings.evidence: At p=0 the GATA1 body center transformed into the unit nuclear-envelope coordinates is (-0.72727,0.6,0.57692), radius 1.1053. 2329/2332 vertices of the box plus zinc-finger decoration lie outside the envelope; the actual box intersects NE triangles through p=0.15. Even at p=0.23, 102 decorative vertices remain outside (max radius 1.02953). This is independent of the earlier chromatin-containment regression, which passes. See diagnostic.json:gata.
findings.whyWrong: The scene identifies GATA1 as the nuclear erythroid regulator and does not depict import. Its visible path goes through intact nuclear membrane on the opposite side from the pore. Even an intended import would need a pore-aligned path instead of a membrane intersection.
findings.fix: Place the complete GATA1 model inside the nuclear envelope throughout its visible regulatory trajectory, including all attached zinc-finger features. If import is intentionally taught instead, supply an explicit aligned pore trajectory; no new process scope is needed here.
findings.verification: Check all visible GATA1 surface vertices and direct triangle intersections against the actual NE for p=0 through 0.46 and both programs; preserve original chromatin/NE and enucleation containment regressions.

sources.supports: Primary structure/abstract describes ER COPII coat assembly, cargo selection and membrane deformation. Used for the conserved membrane-budding requirement, not species-specific MHC biochemistry.

findings.kind: false ER loading/export topology with endpoint discontinuity
findings.location: static ER wall lines 56-96; MHC/carrier and peptide update lines 436-461
findings.evidence: The right ER boundary remains a static continuous wall through the loading and export route. At p=0.46,0.49,0.50,0.52 and 0.54, three peptide-residue meshes intersect actual ER-wall triangles; 16 MHC component meshes intersect at p=0.46, rather than only the transmembrane stalk. The MHC/peptide then travels through that unchanged wall until p≈0.60. A separate endpoint mismatch at p=0.46 moves the peptide origin from (-0.84,0.70,0.12) to (-0.90,0.73,0.12), a 0.0671-unit snap versus bead radius 0.04. Both epitope conditions share this transport path. See diagnostic.json:immuneER.
findings.whyWrong: The peptide groove must face ER lumen during loading, and an integral MHC-I complex must remain embedded in a membrane during vesicular export. The current peptide itself intersects lipid and the carrier crosses an unchanged ER boundary. The compressed-Golgi-route caption does not resolve the false membrane crossing.
findings.fix: Move the loading complex to a real ER membrane site with the entire groove/peptide on the luminal side; provide a continuous preallocated budding/exit geometry before carrier departure. Preserve peptide attachment, membrane orientation, the two recognition branches and existing MHC-groove regression. Match peptide position/orientation exactly at the loading-to-bound transition.
findings.verification: Check actual peptide/groove against ER lipid surfaces through p=0.35-0.62 in both epitope branches; verify membrane continuity during exit and lumen-facing cargo through budding, transport and fusion. Test one-sided position limits at p=0.46 and seek determinism. Root renders normal-distance continuous transport.

findings: ER loading-to-bound origin has a 0.0671-unit position jump at p=0.46; included with issue 03.
Carrier egress crosses an immutable ER wall. The later surface patch switch is explicitly staged around fusion; final TCR engagement and unmatched release have smooth positions.
